submission.justification: T2 has the best nominal resolution (6 um) but is not suitable for the innermost-layer radiation. Its efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm2 is 82%, against the 97% required. Of the two suitable options, T1 resolves better than T3: about 9.2 um against a best of 13.8 um. T1 thickness scan: 150 um gave 9.083 and 9.287 um on repeat, a mean of about 9.19 um. 100 um gave 9.121 um, 130 um gave 9.35 um, 175 um gave 9.363 um, and 200 um gave 9.317 um. 300 um was worse at 11.5 um. Simulation scatter is about 0.2 um, so thicknesses from 100 to 200 um cannot be told apart. 150 um is the best measured point and sits in the middle of the flat optimum. T1 efficiency is 98.5%, above the 97% requirement.

requirements.evidence: T1 at 150 um gives about 9.19 um, the best among the radiation-suitable options. T3 is at best 13.8 um. T2 is better at 6 um but is excluded. The 100-200 um differences are within the 0.2 um scatter.
